questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Amsterdam has one of the largest social science departments in all of europe. It is also a very charming city which I absolutely fell in love with. I also chose Amsterdam because of the short distance from Denmark, and because of the Erasmus grant

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Amsterdam is a diverse city and as an expat you feel welcome there. It was easy for me to feel at home fast.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It wasn't difficult. The University of Amsterdam has an International office which was very good at communicating important information once I arrived in Amsterdam. It was a bit chaotic during the summer holiday but they are generally happy to help at the international student desk.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus Student Network threw a very well organized introduction week where I met so many nice people from around the globe whom I stayed in contact with during the exchange. Once I was enrolled as a student at the UvA, I got registered automatically in the information page for exchange students in Canvas where I received important messages from the International office, for instance an invitation to a welcoming lecture

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: No complaints

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very difficult to find affordable housing in Amsterdam. I would recommend to pay the city a visit so that you can attend viewings and avoid scams. I got the impression that there were extraordinarily many exchange students the semester I was there, and thus nowhere near enough student housing opportunities. You need to be patient and willing to pay a high rent to find a place to live in Amsterdam

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I was having a blast:)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't sign up for student housing because I had the opportunity to share an apartment with a friend. I think that the student accommodation offered by the UvA is pretty expensive too.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The whole mobility online process was overwhelming all the way through the spring semester before going abroad. To be honest it wasn't until the summer holiday started and I was fully enrolled and registered in the right courses that I started to look forward to the actual exchange. But it was definitely worth it:)

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Much of the registration process was handled by mobility online. But then there was some confusion about a language test a few weeks before I was leaving and the course registration process was especially pulling teeth because there was two different systems with different rules (one of them was a raffle of the registered and the other one worked with a first come first served principle) which was very confusing, but the international student service desk was always happy to help and it turned out just fine

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
The international office answered all my questions. 
There was also good information in the introduction week about what other resources was available for students, for instance the UvA offered student counselling or psychological help for those who need it, and there was also an awareness about how Amsterdam is liberal with drugs and which  consequences there can be of that, so exchange students were informed about a rehabilitation center for students too. There is a rich student life among exchange students and lots of activities to join in case you feel lonely or bored.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was lucky enough to get all the courses I registered for but that wasn't the case for everyone I knew.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Keep an eye out for the deadline/ registration dates and be ready by the computer once it opens if you have a course you really want to follow

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I wish I took more courses in my own discipline but the academic level of the courses was generally high and the teachers were good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The work load is about the same as in Denmark but there is different rules about absence and more written assignments than I was used to. Also the grading system is different and the passing grade is much higher than in the Danish system.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: You can really feel there are more resources available. Teachers are more personally related to the students and put a large effort in giving constructive feedback on the work I handed in during the semester.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Secrets of Identity: Knowing others in practice
Bodies in Public 
The Eternal pursuit of happiness: Philosophy, science and technology of well-being

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Secrets of Identity: Knowing others in practice was my favourite course during the stay 
The teacher Annerienke Fioole is super competent and kind, and she made a big deal out of learning everyone's names and overall she facilitated a good learning space. It was a small class / seminar group where I got to know a lot of Dutch people since many of the programmes in the UvA has been made all-English speaking. In the course I was able to do some fieldwork on a topic of choice which was fun.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Event tickets, concert tickets and festivals. If you want to go out you need to pay an entrance fee for a lot of places. Not that the price is high but there is a big event-culture in Amsterdam which means you also kind of need to know what is happening and when, which is kind of difficult if you don't have a network in the city beforehand

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food in grocery stores is cheaper than in DK, especially in the discount supermarkets called Jumbo or Dirk van den Broek. It is also cheaper to go out for drinks at a bar than it is in Copenhagen. The ferry going from central station to Amsterdam Noord is free of charge. Entrance for cultural activities are generally expensive but if you plan to visit a lot of museums you can save some money by buying a museum card (450 DKK)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Erasmus student network had a number of social clubs and activities during the semester for anyone interested. There was also the creative space and student café called CREA which offered courses in dance, drawing, singing, acting etc. for student friendly prices. And the USC is the university sports association where you can join most any type of sports discipline you desire

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined an applied ceramics course in CREA and enjoyed doing something non-academic in my spare time. I also joined the USC fitness membership which was super cheap and accessible and I was happy with their group classes

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to the museums: Van Gogh, Rembrandt huis, Eye film museum, Anne Frank Museum and many more. There is a lot of cute markets around the city where you can buy food, vintage clothing, jewelry and lots of other things: Waterlooplein, Noordermarkt, Albert Cuyp market. During summer definitely go on a canal tour or hang out in the parks with a book. Don't miss the American Book Centre. Enjoy the many cute cafés and bars, take a stroll through the 9 streets and de Jordaan.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, Dutch culture is similar to Danish culture in a lot of ways.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing in particular, but it seems it is not really socially accepted to wear a helmet when you bike which is confusing because the biking paths are busy

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That so many different cultures are represented in the city which made me feel welcome as an expat.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Don't let the application procedure stop you from going abroad! 
Biking is by far the easiest and cheapest way to get around the city 
Join the ESN introduction week in the beginning of the semester

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
I brought my own bike on the Flixbus from Denmark and used it every day. I also knew people who bought a cheap bike when they arrived and sold it when they went back. 
Be careful not to park your bike illegally though. During the first week I unintentionally parked my bike somewhere it was not allowed. My bike was removed by the municipality and put in a site called the 'fietsdepot' around 10 km west of the city centre. I had to go there and pay a fine of 22,5 euros to get it back.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I got to know so many nice people from all around the world and became familiar with the city. I practiced my english skills and tried out other academic disciplines.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To go home :,)

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
